audit_question: After closing the V5 feature-bound dimensional-eligibility seam, does a materially different fresh cross-vendor sample remain predominantly A/B with no comparable recurring C/D pressure, such that portability can become a periodic stress test while catalogue throughput and the demand-side MVP become the primary development focus?
sample_design: disjoint from V1-V5 and their vertical-proof identities
three conventional tethers, two conventional ToolAttachments, one conventional AnchorAttachment, and two composite/system-like tethering products
deliberately avoids another feature-dimension-heavy ToolAttachment slice while retaining enough mechanism/composition diversity to expose a real remaining core seam
decision_basis: The only A case is already representable and ingestible through the unchanged production adapter path.

All seven B cases fit existing product, interface, attachment, anchor-installation, evidence-conflict, assembly/relationship, or manufacturer-declared connection semantics; their remaining work is acquisition/extraction/composition rather than recommendation-core invention.

The two deliberately composite/system-like cases do not justify new runtime primitives before a demand-side use case requires them: one is explicitly a kit of separately catalogued components, while the other can preserve its proprietary transfer behavior as product/connection evidence without changing baseline candidate viability.
No C or D pressure appeared in a materially different post-V5 sample. Portability should remain a periodic regression/stress audit rather than the primary implementation loop.

products.name: Tool tether 15lbs double carabiner
observed_public_facts: 14.99 lb published maximum load / 15 lb product variant
double-carabiner tether
self-locking carabiner wording
shock-absorbing elasticated/bungee tether
core_fit: unknown endpoint roles remain unknown unless stronger evidence establishes direction
products.portability_gap: None. The registered Hilti production adapter already extracts tether capacity, double-carabiner endpoint topology and self-locking connector evidence generically; this fresh identity exercises existing facts and rules without an adapter or core change.

products.name: Wire Tool Lanyard - Loop - 4.5 kg / 10 lbs
observed_public_facts: 1000 mm TPU-coated stainless-steel wire lanyard
65 mm wire loop
Trisafe carabiner with 12 mm hook opening
product title states 4.5 kg / 10 lb while the same page application copy states 6.8 kg / 15 lb maximum dynamic load
evidence_notes: The first-party page contains an exact-product capacity conflict. It must fail closed or be reconciled through ordinary evidence policy; it is not a new capacity semantic.
products.portability_gap: The neutral tether/interface and evidence-conflict model is sufficient. The remaining work is a Dropsafe acquisition/extraction path plus ordinary reconciliation of the contradictory first-party load statements.

products.name: Coil Tool Tether with Swivels and Screw-Gate Carabiners
observed_public_facts: dual stainless-steel screw-gate carabiners
20 in relaxed / 72 in extended coil tether
360 degree heavy-duty swivels
description states 5 lb rating while the same page feature block states 10 lb maximum tool weight
evidence_notes: The first-party page contains an exact-product capacity conflict. Preserve and reconcile it rather than selecting a convenient value.
products.portability_gap: The current Ty-Flot adapter is intentionally scoped to Cold Shrink ToolAttachments rather than this tether family. CC2072 needs Guardian tether ingestion and evidence reconciliation only; its coil, screw-gate, swivel, length and endpoint facts fit existing neutral semantics.

products.name: DBI-SALA D-Ring Attachment with Cord
observed_public_facts: corded D-ring creates a tether attachment point
loop passes through a pre-drilled hole or closed handle and chokes off
2.3 kg / 5 lb maximum capacity
core_fit: captive through-opening OR captive handle eligibility
products.portability_gap: The product maps directly to the existing captive-feature eligibility, cinch/choke and provided-interface semantics. The current 3M adapter is deliberately Quick-Spin-specific, so this is catalogue acquisition/extraction broadening rather than a new primitive.

products.name: 5 lb Tool Attachment with choke-on cinch-loop and aluminum twist-lock carabiner
observed_public_facts: choke-on design for tools with existing captive-eye holes
elastic cinch-loop with nylon cord lock
aluminum twist-lock carabiner provides the tether-side connection
5 lb maximum tool weight
products.portability_gap: This independently reuses the same captive-eye/cinch/connector composition already established by earlier cohorts. The current FallTech ToolAttachment path is Battery-Boot-specific, so 5106A5 needs vendor extraction broadening only.

products.name: Anchor Strap Hook & Loop Closure for Tool Tethering
observed_public_facts: hook-and-loop strap installs around belts, harnesses, railings or other structures
manufacturer instructions bound close-ended installation to a maximum 3 in height and 0.5 in thickness
steel D-ring provides the tether-side interface
2.3 kg / 5 lb maximum capacity
core_fit: existing belt and rail PrimaryAnchorFeature paths
products.portability_gap: The post-PR #62 anchor model can conservatively compile the already-supported belt/rail subsets and their source-bound dimensional constraints without inventing a generic 'structure' or treating every harness segment as a belt. Ergodyne currently has explicit verticals for 3171 and 3178, so 3172 is an ingestion/composition extension, not a new anchor primitive.

products.name: Adjustable Wrist Anchor With Tool Tether - 2.5kg / 5.5lb
observed_public_facts: commercial kit explicitly contains one H01067 Webbing Wrist Tether and one H01085 Slip-On Wrist Anchor
2.5 kg / 5.5 lb published maximum load
wrist-anchor copy permits wrist or hand-rail use
core_fit: separately catalogued tether plus AnchorAttachment components
ordinary candidate composition from component identities
products.portability_gap: The sellable SKU is a kit wrapper, not a new load-path component. Its manufacturer page names the two contained product identities explicitly, so supply-side ingestion should decompose/preserve that assembly relationship and let the existing tether plus AnchorAttachment model reason over the components. A new runtime Composite product primitive is not justified.

products.name: Quick-Switch Link and Dock Pack
observed_public_facts: kit includes one Quick-Switch dock and one tool-tether link
Quick-Switch link plus stainless-steel screw-gate end
6 lb maximum tool weight
manufacturer states tools can be transferred without disconnecting from an anchor while maintaining 100 percent tie-off
core_fit: manufacturer-specific interface type retained as evidence without equating it to a carabiner
standard screw-gate ConnectorSpec on the other end
manufacturer-declared connector/interface compatibility where an exact link/dock relationship is established
products.portability_gap: The proprietary transfer workflow is real product behavior, but it does not need a new baseline recommendation primitive to represent the component identities, load-path interfaces or declared link/dock relationship. Preserve the 100%-tie-off transfer claim as evidence/product behavior and defer dynamic handoff-state reasoning until a demand-side requirement actually needs it. The remaining work is Guardian acquisition/extraction and assembly/compatibility composition.
